course.title: International Integrated Science 9
course.subtitle: Life, Matter, Energy and Earth Systems
course.credit_recommendation: 1 high-school science credit, subject to local law and school policy
course.mapping_status: International benchmark synthesis. Jurisdiction-specific review is required before formal standards or credit reporting.
course.assessment_principle: Every scored item must have one definitive, defensible answer or an explicit evidence-based rubric.
course.current_release: Unit 11 — Space Systems, Astronomy & Cosmic Evidence

mastery_scale.label: Beginning
mastery_scale.description: Needs direct instruction, modeling, and supported practice.

mastery_scale.label: Developing
mastery_scale.description: Shows partial understanding with inconsistent application or evidence.

mastery_scale.label: Proficient
mastery_scale.description: Applies scientific ideas and practices accurately in familiar contexts.

mastery_scale.label: Mastered
mastery_scale.description: Explains, transfers, evaluates, and applies learning in unfamiliar contexts.

units.title: Readiness, Laboratory Safety & Scientific Habits
units.big_idea: Safe, ethical, careful scientific work begins with habits that protect people, evidence, organisms, communities, and environments.

units.title: Scientific Inquiry, Measurement & Evidence
units.big_idea: Scientific explanations become stronger when questions are testable, measurements are reliable, and claims are supported by transparent evidence.

units.title: Cells & the Organization of Life
units.big_idea: Cells are organized systems whose structures and processes make life possible across many scales.
objectives: Explain cell theory and evaluate evidence that living organisms are cellular
Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells without treating either as inferior
Relate major cell structures to their contributions within the whole-cell system
Use microscope scale, image size, actual size, and magnification calculations
Model selective permeability, diffusion, osmosis, and active transport
Explain how surface-area-to-volume ratio constrains cell size and exchange
Connect specialized cells to tissues, organs, and organ systems
Describe photosynthesis and cellular respiration as linked matter and energy processes
Evaluate strengths and limitations of diagrams, models, and microscope images
framework_tags: NGSS: cells, structure and function, hierarchical organization, scientific modeling
Cambridge Biology: organisation of organisms; movement into and out of cells; practical skills
Australian Curriculum: cells, organ systems, inquiry, data interpretation, model evaluation
IB MYP Sciences: knowing and understanding; processing and evaluating
PISA scientific literacy: explain phenomena, evaluate inquiry, interpret evidence

units.title: Body Systems & Homeostasis
units.big_idea: Organ systems interact through feedback and transport processes to maintain stable internal conditions.
objectives: Explain homeostasis as dynamic regulation within functional limits
Model negative feedback using receptors, coordinating centers, effectors, and responses
Trace transport of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, water, ions, hormones, heat, and wastes
Relate structures of the circulatory, respiratory, digestive, urinary, nervous, endocrine, and immune systems to function
Analyze safe physiological-response data without using it to diagnose health conditions
Explain thermoregulation, blood-glucose regulation, and water balance as interacting feedback systems
Compare rapid neural signaling with slower endocrine signaling
Evaluate system models, health claims, uncertainty, and personal-data ethics
framework_tags: NGSS HS-LS1-2 and HS-LS1-3: interacting systems, feedback, and homeostasis
Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 (2026–2028): nutrition, transport, gas exchange, excretion, coordination, immunity, and practical skills
Australian Curriculum Year 9: coordinated and interdependent body systems responding to environmental change
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: systems, inquiry, evidence, evaluation, and impacts

units.title: Cell Division, Reproduction & Inheritance
units.big_idea: Genetic information is copied, expressed, reshuffled, and inherited, producing both continuity and variation.
objectives: Relate DNA, genes, alleles, chromosomes, and genomes across biological scales
Model the cell cycle, DNA replication, mitosis, cytokinesis, growth, repair, and differentiation
Explain how cell-cycle regulation limits uncontrolled division and why simplified cancer models have boundaries
Compare asexual and sexual reproduction in terms of continuity, variation, costs, and context
Model meiosis, homologous chromosome separation, crossing over, independent assortment, and fertilization
Use genotype, phenotype, dominance, codominance, incomplete dominance, and probability accurately
Construct and interpret monohybrid crosses while recognizing that probability does not guarantee family outcomes
Explain mutation and recombination as sources of variation and environment as an influence on trait expression
Evaluate genetic claims, technologies, privacy, consent, uncertainty, and the history of genetic misuse
framework_tags: NGSS HS-LS1-4 and HS-LS3-1–3: mitosis, differentiation, DNA and chromosomes, variation, statistics, and probability
Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610/0970 (2026–2028): reproduction, inheritance, variation, selection, and mathematical/practical skills
Australian Curriculum V9 Year 10 AC9S10U01: mitosis, meiosis, chromosomes, DNA, genes, and Mendelian inheritance
IB MYP Sciences: models, systems, patterns, inquiry, processing, evaluation, and impacts
PISA scientific literacy: explain phenomena, interpret data, evaluate evidence, and communicate uncertainty

units.title: Ecosystems, Evolution & Biodiversity
units.big_idea: Living systems depend on interconnected energy, matter, populations, environments, inherited variation, historical evidence, and responsible stewardship.
objectives: Distinguish organism, population, community, ecosystem, habitat, niche, and biotic and abiotic factors using direct observations
Construct and interpret food chains, food webs, trophic levels, biomass and energy pyramids, and ecological-efficiency calculations
Explain that energy flows through ecosystems while matter cycles through biological, atmospheric, hydrological, and geological reservoirs
Analyze real population records using density, trends, limiting factors, carrying capacity, uncertainty, and alternative explanations
Compare competition, predation, herbivory, mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, disturbance, succession, and resilience
Measure biodiversity using richness, abundance, evenness, sampling design, and a diversity index while protecting sensitive species locations
Explain natural selection as population change across generations involving inherited variation and differential reproductive success
Distinguish microevolution, speciation, and macroevolution, and state what has been directly observed versus historically reconstructed
Evaluate fossils, anatomy, biogeography, genetics, and dating evidence by separating specimens and measurements from classification and ancestry inference
Represent creation, intelligent-design, evolutionary-creation, and naturalistic interpretations accurately while distinguishing empirical, historical, philosophical, and theological claims
Design evidence-based biodiversity conservation or restoration actions that address safety, access, community knowledge, justice, uncertainty, and monitoring
framework_tags: NGSS HS-LS2-1–8: population data, matter and energy, interactions, resilience, group behavior, biodiversity, and design
NGSS HS-LS4-1–6: evidence, variation, natural selection, adaptation, environmental change, and biodiversity solutions
Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610/0970 (2026–2028): variation and selection; organisms and environment; human influences and conservation
Australian Curriculum V9 AC9S9U01 and AC9S10U02: ecosystem interdependence and evidence for evolution by natural selection
Academy enrichment: observation–inference–worldview distinctions and respectful comparative origins literacy

units.title: Atomic Structure & Periodic Patterns
units.big_idea: Element identity, isotope composition, electron arrangements, and periodic position connect invisible atomic structure to measurable patterns in matter.
objectives: Distinguish elements, compounds, and mixtures and connect observable properties to particle-level models
Explain how cathode-ray, scattering, and spectral evidence revised atomic models
State the relative charges, masses, and locations of protons, neutrons, and electrons
Use atomic number, mass number, isotope notation, and charge to determine particle counts
Distinguish isotope mass, mass number, relative atomic mass, and standard atomic weight
Calculate abundance-weighted relative atomic masses from sourced isotope data
Write simplified electron configurations for neutral atoms and ions among elements 1–20
Use spectra as evidence for quantized electron-energy differences while stating model limits
Explain modern atomic-number ordering, periods, groups, and recurring outer-electron patterns
Analyze broad trends for metals, nonmetals, Group 1, Group 17, and Group 18 and make bounded predictions
Evaluate atomic and periodic data sources, model uncertainty, chemical safety, and technological implications
framework_tags: NGSS HS-PS1-1: charged atomic substructure and periodic predictions from outer-electron patterns
Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620/0971 (2026–2028): atomic structure, isotopes, configurations 1–20, and periodic organization
Australian Curriculum V9 Science: chemical structure across subatomic and macroscopic scales, models, evidence, and inquiry
NSW Science Stage 4: periodic-table and atomic-structure data interpretation
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: models, patterns, data, source evaluation, and communication

units.title: Bonding, Chemical Reactions & Matter
units.big_idea: Atoms and ions form structures through electrostatic interactions; chemical reactions rearrange conserved atoms while transferring energy at rates shaped by conditions.
objectives: Explain bonding in terms of electrostatic attraction, electron arrangement, energy, and explicit model limitations
Describe ionic bonding and giant ionic lattices and relate them to melting, brittleness, and conductivity
Construct neutral ionic formulae from monatomic and selected polyatomic ion charges
Describe covalent bonding in simple molecules and distinguish bond strength from intermolecular attraction
Use electronegativity and molecular arrangement to reason qualitatively about bond and molecular polarity
Compare giant covalent, layered covalent, and metallic structures using real property evidence
Translate among names, formulae, relative formula mass, word equations, symbol equations, and state symbols
Balance chemical equations and use atom audits to demonstrate conservation of atoms and mass in closed systems
Evaluate observations as evidence for physical or chemical change and classify useful reaction patterns
Interpret exothermic and endothermic energy pathways, activation energy, bond breaking, bond making, and catalyst effects
Analyze reaction-rate evidence using temperature, concentration, pressure, surface area, catalysts, and collision theory
Describe dynamic equilibrium and evaluate qualitative industrial tradeoffs involving rate, yield, energy, safety, and economics
Use authoritative property, thermochemical, and experimental sources while maintaining chemical-safety boundaries
framework_tags: NGSS HS-PS1-2, HS-PS1-4, HS-PS1-5, and HS-PS1-7: reaction outcomes, energy, rates, and conservation
Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620/0971 (2026–2028): bonding, formulae, equations, energetics, rates, equilibrium, and practical safety
Australian Curriculum chemical science and Year 9 conservation-of-mass inquiry
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: models, evidence, data, risk, uncertainty, and communication

units.title: Motion, Forces & Energy
units.big_idea: Motion changes when net forces act, momentum tracks interactions, and energy is transferred and transformed while remaining conserved within defined systems.
objectives: Use SI units and distinguish scalar from vector quantities
Calculate distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration with stated reference frames and directions
Construct and interpret position–time and velocity–time graphs using slope and area
Identify forces, draw free-body diagrams and calculate one-dimensional net force
Apply Newton’s first, second and third laws without confusing interaction pairs or balanced forces
Distinguish mass from weight and use gravitational field strength near Earth
Calculate momentum and impulse and apply one-dimensional momentum conservation to defined systems
Explain how stopping time affects average force while recognizing broader safety factors
Calculate work, kinetic energy, gravitational potential-energy change, power and efficiency
Track energy transfer, transformation, dissipation and conservation across defined system boundaries
Evaluate real engineering designs using evidence, models, uncertainty, accessibility, tradeoffs and safety
framework_tags: NGSS HS-PS2-1–3: motion data, force–mass–acceleration, momentum and design
NGSS HS-PS3-1–3: energy calculations, system models and design
Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 (2026–2028): motion, forces, momentum, energy, work, power and efficiency
Australian Curriculum V9 physical sciences: forces, motion, energy transfer, transformation and conservation
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: data, models, systems, risk and communication

units.title: Electricity, Waves & Information
units.big_idea: Electrical interactions transfer energy through circuits, magnetic fields connect electricity and motion, and waves carry energy and encoded information through systems with measurable benefits, losses and risks.
objectives: Distinguish charge, current, potential difference, resistance, electrical power and energy
Use Q=It, V=E/Q, V=IR, P=VI and E=Pt with units and stated conditions
Analyze simple series and parallel circuits using current, voltage and equivalent resistance
Interpret current–voltage evidence and distinguish ohmic from changing-resistance behavior
Explain magnetic fields, electromagnets, the motor effect, induction, generators and ideal transformers
Use v=fλ and T=1/f and distinguish amplitude, period, frequency, wavelength and speed
Explain reflection, refraction, diffraction and qualitative superposition
Describe sound transmission, hearing variables and safe exposure evidence
Compare electromagnetic-spectrum regions, applications, benefits and risk controls
Evaluate wave and photon models of electromagnetic radiation
Compare analog and digital signals and evaluate sampling, noise, parity, storage, privacy, security and access
Analyze a communication system from energy source through encoding, channel, receiver and decoding
framework_tags: NGSS HS-PS4-1–3 and HS-PS4-5: wave relationships, digital information, model evidence and communication technologies
Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 (2026–2028): waves, light, sound, magnetism, electricity, circuits, digital electronics and electromagnetic effects
Australian Curriculum V9 Year 9 physical sciences: wave/particle models, energy transfer through media and electric circuits
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: systems, models, data, information, risk and communication

units.title: Earth Systems & Biogeochemical Cycles
units.big_idea: Earth’s internal and solar energy drive interacting geological, hydrological, atmospheric, biological and chemical systems in which matter cycles through reservoirs, feedbacks alter change, and human decisions influence risk and resilience.
objectives: Define Earth-system spheres, reservoirs, fluxes, feedbacks, boundaries and scales
Use seismic, density, magnetic, gravity and laboratory evidence to model Earth’s interior
Connect internal energy, mantle flow and multiple plate-driving processes to lithospheric motion
Use plate-boundary evidence to explain landforms, earthquakes, volcanoes and hazard patterns
Model rock formation, weathering, erosion, transport, deposition and soil development across timescales
Trace water through atmosphere, surface water, soil, ice and groundwater and apply a water budget
Quantify carbon reservoirs, inputs, outputs, net change, fast and slow pathways, and simple residence time
Compare nitrogen and phosphorus cycling and explain nutrient limitation and eutrophication
Use a global-mean energy-balance model to calculate reflection, absorption, outgoing energy and imbalance
Explain the natural greenhouse effect, climate feedbacks, variability, forcing, scenarios and uncertainty
Analyze Earth observations and evaluate hazards, resources, human modifications and technological responses
Design or evaluate resilience and stewardship strategies using safety, justice, access, cultural knowledge and monitoring
framework_tags: NGSS HS-ESS2-1–7: Earth processes, feedbacks, interior evidence, energy flow, carbon cycling and coevolution
NGSS HS-ESS3-1–6: resources, hazards, sustainability, technological solutions, climate data and human modification
Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680: rocks, soils, water, atmosphere, climate, resources, fieldwork and decision-making
Australian Curriculum V9 Earth and space sciences: plate tectonics, carbon cycling and interactions among Earth’s spheres
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: systems, models, evidence, uncertainty, risk and communication

units.title: Space Systems, Astronomy & Cosmic Evidence
units.big_idea: Gravity, radiation and nuclear processes organize space systems, while instruments transform delayed and often indirect signals into evidence about planets, stars, galaxies and cosmic history.
objectives: Use observation frames to explain apparent sky motion, day and night, seasons, lunar phases and eclipses
Use scientific notation, astronomical units, light-time and light-years to compare cosmic scale
Explain orbital motion through gravity, inward acceleration, circular-average speed and energy changes in elliptical paths
Use accretion evidence to explain Solar-System formation and planetary diversity
Describe solar structure, fusion, radiation transfer, solar activity and space-weather effects
Use spectra and telescope wavelength bands to infer composition, temperature, brightness and line-of-sight motion
Model stellar birth, stability, mass-dependent life cycles, remnants and element formation
Evaluate exoplanet transit, radial-velocity and other detection evidence, bias and false positives
Calculate transit depth, radius ratio, spectral redshift, small-shift speed and Hubble-law model values
Place the Solar System within the Milky Way, Local Group and observable universe and explain lookback time
Construct an evidence-based explanation of cosmic expansion and Big Bang theory using redshift, CMB and composition
Evaluate space missions and astronomy claims through uncertainty, processing, debris, planetary protection, access, cultural knowledge, privacy and dual use
framework_tags: NGSS HS-ESS1-1–4 and HS-ESS1-6: solar energy, Big Bang evidence, stellar elements, orbital representations and Solar-System history
Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 (2026–2028): Earth–Moon–Sun motion, Solar System, stars, redshift, CMB and Hubble relationships
Australian Curriculum V9 Year 10 AC9S10U03: Big Bang model, galaxies, stars, solar systems and supporting evidence
IB MYP Sciences and PISA scientific literacy: models, data, uncertainty, technology, ethics and communication

units.title: Sustainable Engineering Capstone
units.big_idea: Engineering uses scientific evidence, criteria, constraints, testing, and revision to improve solutions while accounting for human and environmental consequences.
